question: Which of the following is NOT a name used to refer to the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesopotamian Civilization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Indus-Sarasvati Civilization** is also widely referred to as the **Harappan Civilization** because Harappa was the first site of this ancient culture to be excavated in 1921. *Hence, Option 1 is correct.*
 
• The civilization is often called the **Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilization**, emphasizing the Sarasvati River, which is believed to have been a crucial part of the region's geography during the time. *Hence, Option 3 is correct.*
 
• It is also commonly referred to as the **Indus Civilization**, focusing on the Indus River, where many of its settlements were concentrated. *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*
 
• **Mesopotamian Civilization** is an entirely different ancient civilization located in present-day Iraq, between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. It is distinct from the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization and is not a name used
